text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday.

- According to the newly passed law on ownership and other real rights which is to come into effect on January 1, owners who have purchased their flats from the state will soon also have to buy off the segment of land the flat has been built on.

- Former PM Nikica Valentic's letter forwarded to a number of high-ranking officials regarding the "wheat scandal" in which 45,000 tons of whet have vanished has been leaked to the press. In the letter Valentic tries to clarify his role in the affair.
- Public sector workers protest: Workers asking for wages to go up 58.2 percent, while the government is offering an 11 percent increase.
- EBRD (European Bank for Reconstruction and Development) to invest $4 million in Bank Austria Croatia (BAC).

- The state audit's office investigating how Croatian ministries have helped the 1996 budget go through the roof have found that finances were used for too many business lunches, daily allowances and vehicles.

- The arms destined for the Bosnian Federation that the U.S. ship American Condor brought to the port of Ploce is still sitting in the Croatian port instead of being transported towards Livno and Visoko.

- The dismissed president of the Supreme Court, Krunislav Olujic is preparing his defence following the decision of the State Judicial Council to sack him for alleged involvement in sexual relations with minors and helping those who he knew were linked to criminal activities. -- ZAgreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
